clue.text: (T) Gardens with spades on grass

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting spades on grass sets the suit letter after the slang word

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis, which is also called weed
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gardener is out on the lawn with a couple of spades.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives WEEDS; its first letter sits on the diagonal, where the theme swaps in a letter that makes new real words both ways, so the grid holds HEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed a plot is to tend it, so 'weeds' works as the verb 'gardens'.

clue.text: (A) A criminal might be beaten

definitions.meaning: second meaning: struck with the open hand

explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives CUFFED; its first letter is on the diagonal and the theme turns it to H, so the grid holds HUFFED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuff means both to put handcuffs on a suspect and to hit someone with a blow.

clue.text: (A) Evidence of conflagration caused by topless parliamentarian

indicators.note: topless in a down clue loses the first letter of the word

parts.note: a parliamentarian is a member, as in Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A fire was started by a scantily clad MP.
explanation.walkthrough: EMBER's middle letter is on the diagonal, where the theme gives EMEER, a variant spelling of emir.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing ember left in the ashes is a sign that a fire has burned there.

clue.text: (A) Ditch or trench protecting crown

indicators.note: protecting means the trench word surrounds the crown abbreviation

parts.note: a sap is a covered trench dug towards an enemy position
CR is the abbreviation for crown

explanation.surface: Soldiers dig a ditch or trench to guard the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a noun beside 'trench'; it is the verb, to discard. SCRAP's last letter sits on the diagonal, made G for SCRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to throw it away, and to scrap it means the same.

clue.text: (S) Two actresses holding government memo providing study of waste

indicators.note: holding means the second actress's name keeps the government letter inside it

parts.note: Greta Garbo and Myrna Loy, two Hollywood film stars

explanation.surface: Two film stars clutch an official memo about rubbish research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'memo' is the superfluous word: its first letter M starts the message MAKE NEW REAL WORDS spelt by the extra words in the (S) clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbology is the academic examination of what people throw away, a study of rubbish and refuse.

clue.text: (A) More imposing pair of monarchs

wordplay.note: GR and ER, George Rex and Elizabeth Regina, joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: Two kings together are grander than one.
explanation.walkthrough: GRANDER's last letter falls on the diagonal, where the theme makes it E, giving GRANDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grander is the comparative of grand, meaning more impressive or stately in appearance.

clue.text: (S) If Liberal is right, initiate evil bawdiness

indicators.note: If ... is right asks us to swap the Liberal letter in the word for the right one
is joins the two letters in the swap: the first becomes the second

parts.note: to launch something is to initiate it

explanation.surface: A politician hopes to launch a crusade against bawdy behaviour if the left is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evil' is the superfluous word, supplying E to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunch is earthy sexual explicitness, a near synonym of bawdy vulgarity.

clue.text: (S) Havoc! Afro cult in Ghana keeps hiding

indicators.note: keeps says the run of letters between havoc and Ghana is held there, once the extra word is set aside

parts.note: only the end of havoc belongs to the concealed run
the run continues through cult and in to the first letter of Ghana

explanation.surface: Chaos in Ghana as a cult conceals itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the superfluous 'Afro' (giving A) and the letters run on: havOC CULT IN Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Occulting means concealing or obscuring from view, as an eclipse occults a star.

clue.text: (S) Following orders, old Saint squeezes terribly nice lass

indicators.note: squeezes means the saint's name holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: the Venerable Bede, the Anglo-Saxon monk and historian, is a saint

indicators.note: terribly signals the word nice is muddled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An ancient holy man hugging a pleasant girl did just as he was told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lass' is the superfluous word, giving L to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance with commands, the state of doing what one is told.

clue.text: (S) John's partner's three-quarters Native American and a champion weirdo

parts.note: Yoko Ono was John Lennon's partner

indicators.note: three-quarters keeps three of the four letters of the tribe name

parts.note: the Zuni are a Pueblo people of New Mexico
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale of Yoko Ono, a Native American and an eccentric champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The word in the sumo sense: a yokozuna holds sumo wrestling's highest rank. 'weirdo' is the superfluous word, giving W.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokozuna is the title of a grand champion in Japanese sumo wrestling.

clue.text: (T) Leaflet with bit of fun that is splitting sides

indicators.note: a bit of the word fun is just its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written; only its first letter is used

indicators.note: splitting means the abbreviation for that is goes between the two side letters

parts.note: L and R, left and right, are the two sides
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A comic pamphlet so funny it has readers splitting their sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives FLIER; its middle letter is on the diagonal, where the theme makes a new real word, so the grid holds FLEER (to mock).
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a handbill or printed sheet handed out for advertising, the same thing as a leaflet.

clue.text: (S) Shakespearean character: fit, aloof and something of an ass!

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever and shivering
a cheek is one half of the backside, so part of an ass

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare role described as moody, distant and rather foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Andrew Aguecheek is the foolish knight in Twelfth Night, so 'something of an ass' fits him too. 'aloof' is the superfluous word, giving A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Andrew Aguecheek is a comic figure in Twelfth Night, one of Shakespeare's characters.

clue.text: (T) Spenser's implanted people in the midst of death

definitions.note: Spenser used enrace to mean implant, so this is the archaic past participle

indicators.note: in the midst of puts the word for people inside the word for death

parts.note: end is a common word for death
a race is a people

explanation.surface: A line about souls planted among the dying, in the old poet's style.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet, used ENRACE for 'implant'. Its fifth letter lies on the diagonal, where the theme swaps in G for ENRAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Faerie Queene the verb enrace means to plant or root in, so enraced equals implanted.

clue.text: (S) Mostly eccentric knight following mountain pass from which it was hard to escape

definitions.text: from which it was hard to escape

indicators.note: following places the shortened eccentric word after the pass

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: ditzy means scatterbrained or eccentric

explanation.surface: An odd knight crosses a mountain pass into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: Colditz Castle was the German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War, famed for escape attempts. 'knight' is the superfluous word, giving K.
explanation.definitionFit: Colditz Castle held Allied officers judged escape risks, and breaking out of it was notoriously difficult.

clue.text: (T) Hired to pen lines lacking oomph

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the word for hired wraps round the lines

parts.note: someone hired is paid

explanation.surface: A hack writer, paid to churn out verse, produces something limp.
explanation.walkthrough: PALLID's fifth letter is on the diagonal; the theme turns it to E, giving PALLED in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid writing or performance is insipid and colourless, without vigour or energy.

clue.text: (S) Over-the-top magazine is flat

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an apartment on the top floor of a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is the superfluous word, giving O; 'the-top' hints that the flat is at the top of a block.
explanation.definitionFit: Penthouse names both a glossy adult magazine and a luxury apartment on a building's top storey.

clue.text: (S) Almost all rich maidens going crazy for him?

definitions.note: the definition is a hint at a man the maidens are crazy about

indicators.note: going crazy signals the combined letters are scrambled
almost drops the last letter of all

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Nearly every wealthy young woman is mad about this fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich' is the superfluous word, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a womaniser, the sort of fellow young women are said to fall for.

clue.text: (S) Cute Elizabeth is mooning terribly having forsaken love

indicators.note: terribly tells us the remaining letters are jumbled
having forsaken means one letter is left out of the word mooning

parts.note: taken as written, before a letter is dropped
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Pretty Elizabeth is pining badly after being dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elizabeth' is the superfluous word, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignon, borrowed from French, means small and delicately pretty, so it is dainty and sweet.

clue.text: (S) Dice game thus disheartened mob

indicators.note: disheartened removes the middle letter of the word for thus

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written
a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A dice game reduces a gang to despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dice' is the superfluous word, giving D; Scrabble is a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the popular board game of forming words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: (S) Country in Central America with nothing nice

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America
nada is Spanish for nothing, common in English slang

explanation.surface: A Central American nation turns out to have nothing pleasant about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central America' tempts one to name a country there; it supplies only the abbreviation. 'nice' is the superfluous word, giving N.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is the North American nation north of the United States.

clue.text: (T) Former Tory leader heading off to pursue spin in the capital

indicators.note: to pursue means the leader's shortened name comes after the spin letters

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the leader's surname

parts.note: William Hague led the Conservative Party from 1997 to 2001

explanation.surface: A deposed Conservative chief chases publicity in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for the UK Conservative Party. PRAGUE's second letter sits on the diagonal, where the theme swaps in L for PLAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic, so 'the capital' names it in context.

clue.text: (A) Earthenware ‚Ä° la JK Rowling?

parts.note: Rowling is the author of the Harry Potter books
à la means in the style of, as the suffix -y makes a word mean like something

explanation.surface: A question of whether the Harry Potter author is a ceramics fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The source garbles 'à la' as '‚Ä° la'. POTTERY's first letter is on the diagonal, made L for LOTTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthenware is fired clay ware, which is the material and craft of pottery.

clue.text: (S) Small, loathsome, tailless, sinister insect

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small

indicators.note: tailless cuts the final letter off the word

parts.note: vile means loathsome

explanation.surface: A description of a tiny, hateful, sinister bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' is the superfluous word, giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout, a pest of grain and crops.

clue.text: (A) Bloomers producing excited stares

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the word stares is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone in baggy underwear draws excited stares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like knickers; here it means flowers. ASTERS ends on the diagonal, where N makes ASTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like garden flowers, things that bloom, so they are bloomers.

clue.text: (S) Entrap runner in obstacle during running heat

indicators.note: during puts the obstacle word inside the rearranged heat letters
running makes the letters of heat move about

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
let is an old word for a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Trapping a sprinter at a hurdle during a race heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrap' is the superfluous word, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a sportsperson, and a runner is the commonest kind on the track.

clue.text: (T) Spartan trained horses

indicators.note: trained says the letters of Spartan are drilled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A warrior from Sparta has schooled his cavalry mounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' looks like the definition; it is the fodder. TARPANS has its third letter on the diagonal, made I for TAIPANS.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpan is the extinct wild horse of the Eurasian steppes, so tarpans are a breed of horse.

clue.text: (A) Forward! Mount an attack!

parts.note: the cry 'On!' urges people forward
to set a jewel is to mount it

explanation.surface: A commander's battle cry ordering the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: ONSET begins on the diagonal; the theme makes it I, so the grid holds INSET.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault, as in the first onset of the enemy, so it is an attack.

clue.text: (A) Rector, tucking into an alcoholic drink, is smiling

indicators.note: the rector's letter tucks into the drink, going inside it

parts.note: a gin, written as one string

explanation.surface: The vicar beams as he works through a glass of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating or drinking; it places one piece inside. AGRIN's middle letter is on the diagonal, made A for AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrin is a literary adverb for grinning, so it means wearing a broad smile.

clue.text: (S) Imbue love wildly in this bit of Welsh 5?

definitions.note: 5 is 5 Down, bawdiness; with Welsh superfluous, the answer is a piece of bawdiness

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of imbue love are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A wild romance in a corner of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' is the superfluous word, giving W; without it the definition reads 'this bit of 5', a bit of bawdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue movie is a pornographic film, a piece of crude explicit entertainment.

clue.text: (T) About to cut painful gash

indicators.note: the short word for about cuts into the painful word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a sore spot is a painful one
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of slicing a nasty wound.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE's middle letter lies on the diagonal; the theme makes it A, giving SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a scratch or incised line, the same kind of cut as a gash.

clue.text: (S) Rabbi always runs away from genuinely hugging bird

indicators.note: hugging means the shortened word wraps round the bird
away from takes the runs letter out of the word for genuinely

parts.note: really means genuinely
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A rabbi always flees genuine embraces with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs. 'Rabbi' is the superfluous word, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, without end, so it is a synonym of always.

clue.text: (T) Singer's number, Love by Queen

indicators.note: by means beside, so the queen letter is placed next to love

parts.note: ten is a number
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
R is regina, queen

explanation.surface: A vocalist's song is a love ballad by the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: TENOR's last letter is on the diagonal, made N to give TENON in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male vocalist with a high voice, so the word names a kind of singer.
